result.topic_en: Euler corrects the tabular longitude of the lunar node and the orbital inclination from an eclipse, then sets up a new method using the initial, final and immersion times of a total lunar eclipse to determine the node distance, the inclination and the remaining unknown.
result.transcription:
De vero loco nodi atque vera inclinatione orbitae lunaris ad eclipticam. 381
[...] longitudo nodi vera hoc tempore non $9^s 8^0 8' 52''$, ut tabulae praebent, sed $9^s 8^0 12' 15''$ sci-
licet $3' 23''$ [?] promotior esse debebat. Hinc ergo longitudo media nodi tabularis $3' 23''$ augeri debere
[...] cum ante augmentum $5' 47''$ esset inventum; ita ut vix dubitari liceat, quin ad longitudi-
nes nodi in tabulis exhibitas nonnulla minuta prima adjici debeant. Hinc autem porro ob angulos
[...] $x = -10^0 30' 6''$ et $x - b = -10^0 8' 23''$ reperitur certius $l\sin^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho = 7,3218378$,
[...] $\frac{1}{2}\varrho = 8,6609189$ et $\frac{1}{2}\varrho = 2^0 37' 21''$, et hoc tempore inclinatio $\varrho = 5^0 14' 42''$, quae a tabu-
lis deficit $1' 47''$.
§. 10. Verumtamen ob hoc ipsum, quod hic tantum initium ac finis eclipsis in calculum indu-
cuntur, huic determinationi non admodum confidere licet; propterea quod reipsa tres habemus quan-
titates incognitas $x$, $\varrho$ et $c$, ad quas definiendas duae aequationes ex initio ac fine eclipsis deductae
non sufficiunt. Etsi enim valorem ipsius $c$ hic jam tanquam cognitum assumsimus, notandum tamen
est ex minimo errore in eo commisso errores satis grandes in determinationes arcuum $x$ et $\varrho$ irrepere
posse. Vulgo quidem, si eclipsis partialis adhibetur, quantitas maximae obscurationis insuper in
subsidium vocari solet, quae quoniam per observationem exactissime assignari nequit, expedire vide-
tur eclipsibus totalibus, in quibus tam initium ac finis, quam immersio et emersio omni cura sunt
observata, ad hoc institutum uti. Ne autem summa formularum supra inventarum complicatio
calculum impediat, ternas aequationes, quas observationes initii, finis et immersionis suppeditant
contemplemur, aliamque methodum aperiamus, ex iis immediate quantitates incognitas $x$, $\varrho$ et $c$
determinandi.
§. 11. Sit tempore eclipsis medio motus solis horarius $= m$
motus lunae horarius $= n$
motus nodi horarius $= k = 8$
semidiameter umbrae $= \alpha$ \} $\alpha + \beta = f$
semidiameter lunae $= \beta$ \} $\alpha - \beta = F$
tempus ab initio eclipsis ad finem elapsum $= h$ hor.
tempus ab immersione ad emersionem $= H$ hor.
ponaturque $a = \frac{1}{2}h(n+k)$ $A = \frac{1}{2}H(n+k)$
$b = \frac{1}{2}h(m+k)$ $B = \frac{1}{2}H(m+k)$
Tum sint incognitae quantitates
distantia nodi ☊ a centro umbrae $= x$
distantia nodi ☊ a centro lunae $= y$
inclinatio orbitae lunaris ad eclipt. $= \varrho$
atque habebuntur hae aequalitates
$\cos\varrho = \frac{\cos f - \cos(y-a)\cos(x-b)}{\sin(y-a)\sin(x-b)} = \frac{\cos f - \cos(y+a)\cos(x+b)}{\sin(y+a)\sin(x+b)}$
longque [?]
$\cos\varrho = \frac{\cos F - \cos(y-A)\cos(x-B)}{\sin(y-A)\sin(x-B)} = \frac{\cos F - \cos(y+A)\cos(x+B)}{\sin(y+A)\sin(x+B)}$

items.quote: ita ut vix dubitari liceat, quin ad longitudines nodi in tabulis exhibitas nonnulla minuta prima adjici debeant
items.english: so that one can hardly doubt that some minutes of arc must be added to the longitudes of the node shown in the tables

items.quote: notandum tamen est ex minimo errore in eo commisso errores satis grandes in determinationes arcuum $x$ et $\varrho$ irrepere posse
items.english: it should be noted, however, that from the smallest error committed in it, quite large errors can creep into the determinations of the arcs x and ρ

items.quote: ternas aequationes, quas observationes initii, finis et immersionis suppeditant contemplemur, aliamque methodum aperiamus, ex iis immediate quantitates incognitas $x$, $\varrho$ et $c$ determinandi
items.english: let us consider the three equations furnished by observations of the beginning, end and immersion, and reveal another method of determining from them directly the unknown quantities x, ρ and c
